html:
A video from Facebook Reality Labs on the future of audio in augmented-reality glasses, with Fanyu Meng’s reading of the key technologies involved: beamforming, machine learning and active noise cancellation.

The AR glasses would carry many microphones and use beamforming to scan for sound sources, rather like radar. But when several sources are competing, which one do you want to hear? Sensors on the glasses track your head and eye movements to work out which sound you are interested in, and that, he notes, must involve machine learning. Active noise cancellation, he guesses, would then suppress the other, interfering sources once the main source has been identified. Beamforming serves the same purpose, so combining the two should work better than either alone.

Ideally, as the video shows, you could follow what the person across the table is saying in a noisy bar without having to lean in cheek to cheek.

Video: Facebook Reality Labs, via oculus.com; shared by Fanyu Meng on Ziyu Acoustics.
